This does not mean every education-related debt qualifies. The three exclusion-ground alternatives remain separate: the first two use their specified HEA discharge paths, while only the third prints otherwise discharged on account of death or total and permanent disability of the student. A parent borrower is not silently equated to the student. Full 437(a) retains qualifying loans, death/disability determinations, safeguards, conditional reinstatement, VA documentation and own income-monitoring/approval/opt-out/update rules; 437(d) separately addresses a parent loan when the student dies. Captured 464(c)(1)(F) retains loan-fund agreement scope, borrower death, regulated permanent/total disability, the medically determinable substantial-gainful-activity alternative with its own duration/death tests, and VA unemployability due to service-connected disability. Part D parallel benefit is retained with complete captured 455 and its unless-otherwise-specified limitation, not a universal cancellation promise. Tax exclusion after a qualifying discharge is distinct from authority to cancel a loan. Both versions define the SSN by 24(h)(7), with their own same-bill amended definition and previously bound SSA issuance authority: citizen or the specified authorization route, and issuance before the return due date, not a bare identification number or a citizen-only rule. No child-credit amount or qualifying-child requirement is imported into the loan exclusion. Math-error treatment retains the existing notice and conditional abatement/deficiency procedure, including the 60-day abatement-request path; it is not a fraud finding or actual assessment. The effective date is discharges after December 31, 2025, not taxable years beginning after that date. No individual exclusion, discharge, marital status, SSA-number validity or return result is inferred. Senate requires the taxpayer SSN on the return and does not print the House conditional-spouse requirement or similar-32(d) addition. Those House clauses are not borrowed. Senate further amends the as-amended math-error list by adding (X), not House (W). House application question 54 is not treated as a settled Senate marital rule. Other H.R.1 components and all separately reserved application questions remain unfinished. Selected exact Senate account and separate pilot eligibility clauses follow. Senate 70204 IRA treatment with own exceptions: Except as provided in this section or under regulations or guidance established by the Secretary, a Trump account shall be treated for purposes of this title in the same manner as an individual retirement account under section 408(a). Senate 70204 account establishment and instrument: The term `Trump account' means an individual retirement account (as defined in section 408(a)) which is not designated as a Roth IRA and which meets the following requirements: (A) The account-- (i) is created or organized by the Secretary for the exclusive benefit of an eligible individual or such eligible individual's beneficiaries, or (ii) is-- (I) created or organized in the United States for the exclusive benefit of an individual who has not attained the age of 18 before the end of the calendar year, or such individual's beneficiaries, and (II) funded by a qualified rollover contribution. (B) The account is designated (in such manner as the Secretary shall prescribe) at the time of the establishment of the account as a Trump account. (C) The written governing instrument creating the account meets the following requirements: (i) No contribution will be accepted-- (I) before the date that is 12 months after the date of the enactment of this section, or (II) in the case of a contribution made in any calendar year before the calendar year in which the account beneficiary attains age 18, if such contribution would result in aggregate contributions (other than exempt contributions) for such calendar year in excess of the contribution limit specified in subsection (c)(2)(A). (ii) Except as provided in subsection (d), no distribution will be allowed before the first day of the calendar year in which the account beneficiary attains age 18. (iii) No part of the account funds will be invested in any asset other than an eligible investment during any period before the first day of the calendar year in which the account beneficiary attains age 18. Senate 70204 eligible individual and reciprocal election paths: The term `eligible individual' means any individual-- (A) who has not attained the age of 18 before the close of the calendar year in which the election under subparagraph (C) is made, (B) for whom a social security number (within the meaning of section 24(h)(7)) has been issued before the date on which an election under subsection (C) is made, and (C) for whom-- (i) an election is made under this subparagraph by the Secretary if the Secretary determines (based on information available to the Secretary from tax returns or otherwise) that such individual meets the requirements of subparagraphs (A) and (B) and no prior election has been made for such individual under clause (ii), or (ii) an election is made under this subparagraph by a person other than the Secretary (at such time and in such manner as the Secretary may prescribe) for the establishment of a Trump account if no prior election has been made for such individual under clause (i). Senate 70204 account beneficiary: The term `account beneficiary' means the individual on whose behalf the Trump account was established. Senate 70204 full-balance account rollover: For purposes of this section, the term `qualified rollover contribution' means an amount which is paid in a direct trustee-to-trustee transfer from a Trump account maintained for the benefit of the account beneficiary to a Trump account maintained for such beneficiary, but only if the amount of such payment is equal to the entire balance of the Trump account from which the payment is made. Senate 70204 elected child payment: In the case of an individual who makes an election under this section with respect to an eligible child of the individual, such eligible child shall be treated as making a payment against the tax imposed by subtitle A (for the taxable year for which the election was made) in an amount equal to $1,000. Senate 70204 refund to child account: The amount treated as a payment under subsection (a) shall be paid by the Secretary to the Trump account with respect to which such eligible child is the account beneficiary. Senate 70204 pilot birth window, no prior election and citizenship: For purposes of this section, the term `eligible child' means a qualifying child (as defined in section 152(c))-- (1) who is born after December 31, 2024, and before January 1, 2029, (2) with respect to whom no prior election has been made under this section by such individual or any other individual, and (3) who is a United States citizen. Senate 70204 pilot election administration: An election under this section shall be made at such time and in such manner as the Secretary shall provide. Senate 70204 pilot child identification and election-date definition: (1) In general.--This section shall not apply to any taxpayer unless such individual includes with the election made under this section the social security number of the eligible child with respect to whom the election is made. (2) Social security number defined.--For purposes of paragraph (1), the term `social security number' shall have the meaning given such term in section 24(h)(7), determined by substituting `before the date of the election made under section 6434' for `before the due date of such return' in subparagraph (B) thereof. Senate 70204 payment offset exception: Any payment made to any individual under this section shall not be-- (1) subject to reduction or offset pursuant to subsection (c), (d), (e), or (f) of section 6402 or any similar authority permitting offset, or (2) reduced or offset by other assessed Federal taxes that would otherwise be subject to levy or collection. Senate 70204 payment interest start: The period determined under section 6611(a) with respect to any payment under this section shall not begin before January 1, 2028. Senate 70204 mirror-code election: In the case of any possession of the United States with a mirror code tax system (as defined in section 24(k)), this section shall not be treated as part of the income tax laws of the United States for purposes of determining the income tax law of such possession unless such possession elects to have this section be so treated. Senate 70204 pilot account definitions: For purposes of this section, the terms `Trump account' and `account beneficiary' have the meaning given such terms in section 530A(b).. Senate 70204 improper-election penalty and incorporated definitions: In the case of any individual who makes an election under section 6434 with respect to an individual who is not an eligible child of the taxpayer-- (1) if such election was made due to negligence or disregard of the rules or regulations, there shall be imposed a penalty of $500, or (2) if such election was made due to fraud, there shall be imposed a penalty of $1,000. (b) Definitions.-- (1) Eligible child.--The term `eligible child' has the meaning given such term under section 6434. (2) Negligence; disregard.--The terms `negligence' and `disregard' have the same meaning as when such terms are used in section 6662.. Senate 70204 math-error amendment: Section 6213(g)(2), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, is amended by striking and at the end of subparagraph (Y), by striking the period at the end of subparagraph (Z) and inserting , and, and by inserting after subparagraph (Z) the following new subparagraph: (AA) an omission of a correct social security number required under section 6434(e)(1) (relating to the Trump accounts contribution pilot program).. Senate 70204 tax-year applicability: The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025. Senate 70204 Treasury administration appropriation: In addition to amounts otherwise available, there is appropriated to the Department of the Treasury, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, $410,000,000, to remain available until September 30, 2034, to carry out the amendments made by this section. Account creation and pilot contribution eligibility are separate. The account-only clauses above do not print the pilot citizenship test, and the candidate does not import that test to every account. Nor does a trust organized in the United States establish the birthplace or citizenship of an account beneficiary. Each pilot retains its own birth window after December 31, 2024 and before January 1, 2029, qualifying-child reference and account-only payment; a birth window does not mean a United States birthplace. Complete original 152 definitions, exceptions, qualifying-child relationship, residence, age, self-support and joint-return conditions, tie-breakers, divorced-parent alternatives, adoption/foster-child definitions and limited missing-child rule are bound. No automatic parent claim, universal child entitlement or taxpayer citizenship classification is inferred. The defined-number references use their own same-bill 24(h)(7) and complete SSA issuance route, citizen or specified authorization, with each applicable issuance deadline retained. Number validity is distinct from citizenship and from all remaining eligibility requirements. No child-credit amount or earlier loan-exclusion similar-32(d) marital clause is imported into the pilot. Existing notice, 60-day conditional abatement-request and deficiency context remains separate from the new math-error list addition. The new fixed-dollar negligence/fraud alternatives incorporate only 6662 definitions, not its 20-percent penalty; no actual negligence, fraud, assessment or payment is inferred. General retirement/investment/distribution/employer-contribution and unrelated tax mechanics outside the selected clauses remain bound section context, not fully interpreted component claims. Other H.R.1 components and separately reserved application questions remain unfinished. Senate account eligible-individual requirements retain the end-of-election-year under-18 test, defined SSN issued before the election and reciprocal Secretary/person-other-than-Secretary election paths with their own prior-election conditions. The alternative account-creation path requires United States organization, own year-end age test and a qualified rollover that transfers the entire balance. General IRA treatment is subject to new 530A and Secretary regulations/guidance, is not Roth treatment, and is not the House independent trust regime. Senate contributions begin 12 months after enactment, and its distributions use the first day of the age-18 calendar year with own subsection (d) exceptions, not the House birthday/under-25 rule. Pilot separately requires a qualifying child within the birth window, no prior election by this or any other individual and United States citizenship; it does not print House citizenship-at-birth wording. Child SSN accompanies the pilot election with an express before-election substitution in the definition, without House taxpayer/spouse SSNs or a return-only requirement. The separate account before-election condition and unmodified 24(h)(7) return-due-date definition are both retained; actual combined timing/application is reserved as question 57. Tax years beginning after December 31, 2025, account contribution start, interest period not before January 1, 2028 and Treasury $410 million administration availability until September 30, 2034 are separate dates/purposes, not interchangeable child-payment deadlines or benefits. Selected exact Senate tips and overtime deduction/identification clauses follow. Senate 70201 deduction and reporting gate: There shall be allowed as a deduction an amount equal to the qualified tips received during the taxable year that are included on statements furnished to the individual pursuant to section 6041(d)(3), 6041A(e)(3), 6050W(f)(2), or 6051(a)(18), or reported by the taxpayer on Form 4137 (or successor). Senate 70201 amount and income limits: (1) In general.--The amount allowed as a deduction under this section for any taxable year shall not exceed $25,000. (2) Limitation based on adjusted gross income.-- (A) In general.--The amount allowable as a deduction under subsection (a) (after application of paragraph (1)) shall be reduced (but not below zero) by $100 for each $1,000 by which the taxpayer's modified adjusted gross income exceeds $150,000 ($300,000 in the case of a joint return). (B) Modified adjusted gross income.--For purposes of this paragraph, the term `modified adjusted gross income' means the adjusted gross income of the taxpayer for the taxable year increased by any amount excluded from gross income under section 911, 931, or 933. Senate 70201 non-employee business-income limit: In the case of qualified tips received by an individual during any taxable year in the course of a trade or business (other than the trade or business of performing services as an employee) of such individual, such qualified tips shall be taken into account under subsection (a) only to the extent that the gross income for the taxpayer from such trade or business for such taxable year (including such qualified tips) exceeds the sum of the deductions (other than the deduction allowed under this section) allocable to the trade or business in which such qualified tips are received by the individual for such taxable year. Senate 70201 qualified-tip conditions: For purposes of this section-- (1) In general.--The term `qualified tips' means cash tips received by an individual in an occupation which customarily and regularly received tips on or before December 31, 2024, as provided by the Secretary. (2) Exclusions.--Such term shall not include any amount received by an individual unless-- (A) such amount is paid voluntarily without any consequence in the event of nonpayment, is not the subject of negotiation, and is determined by the payor, (B) the trade or business in the course of which the individual receives such amount is not a specified service trade or business (as defined in section 199A(d)(2)), and (C) such other requirements as may be established by the Secretary in regulations or other guidance are satisfied. For purposes of subparagraph (B), in the case of an individual receiving tips in the trade or business of performing services as an employee, such individual shall be treated as receiving tips in the course of a trade or business which is a specified service trade or business if the trade or business of the employer is a specified service trade or business. (3) Cash tips.--For purposes of paragraph (1), the term `cash tips' includes tips received from customers that are paid in cash or charged and, in the case of an employee, tips received under any tip-sharing arrangement. Senate 70201 identification: (1) In general.--No deduction shall be allowed under this section unless the taxpayer includes on the return of tax for the taxable year such individual's social security number. (2) Social security number defined.--For purposes of paragraph (1), the term `social security number' shall have the meaning given such term in section 24(h)(7). Senate 70201 own married-individual joint-return rule: If the taxpayer is a married individual (within the meaning of section 7703), this section shall apply only if the taxpayer and the taxpayer's spouse file a joint return for the taxable year. Senate 70201 anti-reclassification regulations: The Secretary shall prescribe such regulations or other guidance as may be necessary to prevent reclassification of income as qualified tips, including regulations or other guidance to prevent abuse of the deduction allowed by this section. Senate 70201 deduction termination: No deduction shall be allowed under this section for any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2028.. Senate 70201 non-itemizer deduction: Section 63(b) is amended by striking and at the end of paragraph (3), by striking the period at the end of paragraph (4) and inserting , and, and by adding at the end the following new paragraph: (5) the deduction provided in section 224.. Senate 70201 math-error amendment: Section 6213(g)(2), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, is amended by striking and at the end of subparagraph (W), by striking the period at the end of subparagraph (X) and inserting , and, and by inserting after subparagraph (X) the following new subparagraph: (Y) an omission of a correct social security number required under section 224(e) (relating to deduction for qualified tips).. Senate 70201 tax-year applicability: The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024. Senate 70202 deduction and reporting gate: There shall be allowed as a deduction an amount equal to the qualified overtime compensation received during the taxable year and included on statements furnished to the individual pursuant to section 6041(d)(4) or 6051(a)(19). Senate 70202 amount and income limits: (1) In general.--The amount allowed as a deduction under this section for any taxable year shall not exceed $12,500 ($25,000 in the case of a joint return). (2) Limitation based on adjusted gross income.-- (A) In general.--The amount allowable as a deduction under subsection (a) (after application of paragraph (1)) shall be reduced (but not below zero) by $100 for each $1,000 by which the taxpayer's modified adjusted gross income exceeds $150,000 ($300,000 in the case of a joint return). (B) Modified adjusted gross income.--For purposes of this paragraph, the term `modified adjusted gross income' means the adjusted gross income of the taxpayer for the taxable year increased by any amount excluded from gross income under section 911, 931, or 933. Senate 70202 qualified-overtime conditions: (1) In general.--For purposes of this section, the term `qualified overtime compensation' means overtime compensation paid to an individual required under section 7 of the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 that is in excess of the regular rate (as used in such section) at which such individual is employed. (2) Exclusions.--Such term shall not include any qualified tip (as defined in section 224(d)). Senate 70202 identification: (1) In general.--No deduction shall be allowed under this section unless the taxpayer includes on the return of tax for the taxable year such individual's social security number. (2) Social security number defined.--For purposes of paragraph (1), the term `social security number' shall have the meaning given such term in section 24(h)(7). Senate 70202 own married-individual joint-return rule: If the taxpayer is a married individual (within the meaning of section 7703), this section shall apply only if the taxpayer and the taxpayer's spouse file a joint return for the taxable year. Senate 70202 regulations: The Secretary shall issue such regulations or other guidance as may be necessary or appropriate to carry out the purposes of this section, including regulations or other guidance to prevent abuse of the deduction allowed by this section. Senate 70202 deduction termination: No deduction shall be allowed under this section for any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2028.. Senate 70202 non-itemizer deduction: Section 63(b), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, is amended by striking and at the end of paragraph (4), by striking the period at the end of paragraph (5) and inserting , and, and by adding at the end the following new paragraph: (6) the deduction provided in section 225.. Senate 70202 math-error amendment: Section 6213(g)(2), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, is amended by striking and at the end of subparagraph (X), by striking the period at the end of subparagraph (Y) and inserting , and, and by inserting after subparagraph (Y) the following new subparagraph: (Z) an omission of a correct social security number required under section 225(d) (relating to deduction for qualified overtime).. Senate 70202 tax-year applicability: The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024. These provisions allow deductions for their own qualified income, not exemption of every dollar described colloquially as tips or overtime and not a guarantee of zero tax. Each retains the complete printed qualified-income gates and its own new statutory subsection references; statements/Form 4137 references, business net-income limits, exceptions and regulatory instructions are not omitted. The original 199A(d)(2) service-business definition is bound with its own 1202/475 references, without importing the separate 199A(d)(3) qualified-business-income phase-in as an automatic tips exception or classifying an actual profession. Overtime means compensation required under FLSA section 7 in excess of the regular rate, not all compensation for hours described as overtime or a taxpayer employment determination. Complete original section 7 with common applicability, regular-rate inclusions/exclusions, alternative arrangements, compensatory-time and other own limitations is bound; no universal 40-hour or all-worker eligibility claim is inferred. All four SSN definitions use their own same-bill 24(h)(7) and full SSA issuance route: citizen or specified authorization, issued before the return due date, not every SSN or a citizen-only rule. Neither a valid number nor filing alone establishes the deduction. Own non-itemizer allowance and math-error amendment remain distinct from existing notice, conditional 60-day abatement-request and deficiency procedure; no actual assessment/fraud determination. All four deduction sections apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024, and deny deductions for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2028; tax-year language is not a discharge/event deadline or repeal of all related reporting/business-credit rules. Other financial/reporting context remains in complete source bindings without an actual implementation conclusion. Other H.R.1 components and separately reserved questions remain unfinished. Senate tips and overtime require taxpayer SSN, without a separately printed House spouse-SSN condition or similar-32(d) addition. Each independently requires a joint return if the taxpayer is married within 7703. Complete original 7703 retains end-of-year or death timing, legal-separation rule and its living-apart alternative requiring a separate return, own household/child/dependency conditions, over-half household costs and no spouse membership during the final six months. No blanket joint filing for every person colloquially described as married. Senate tips caps deduction at $25,000; overtime at $12,500 or $25,000 for a joint return, each with $100 per $1,000 over $150,000/$300,000 MAGI phaseout and own 911/931/933 additions. Senate tips uses own cash/charged/tip-sharing and employee/employer service-business clauses; overtime excludes qualified tips, without importing House highly-compensated/earned-income exclusions. Senate inserts math-error (Y) for tips and (Z) for overtime. No House spouse, similar-marital, compensation-threshold, extra-quote or distinct qualified-tip subsection rule is borrowed.

The Clerk recorded the House result as 'Passed' on 2025-07-03. This does not establish enactment.

- Selected source-bound Immigration highlights, not an exhaustive package or immigration-component inventory. The whole reconciliation measure also addresses taxes, benefits, defense, education, energy and other policies; a package vote cannot establish a separate position on any highlighted or omitted component.
- House70101 prints a State-licensing-independent family-center definition and SOLE discretion over single-adult standards. It cannot be replaced by Senate90003's differently qualified text. Detention-law/judicial interactions require separate review; no universal custody duty, individual removal or legal enforceability ruling is inferred.
- All listed appropriations are additional fiscal2025 amounts with September30,2029 availability. The State reimbursement provision requires costs associated with actions taken on or after January21,2021 and satisfactory evidence of costs incurred and bars specified duplicate DHS reimbursement. Availability is not actual spending, awards, detention or removal.
- Asylum filing and yearly pending-application fees are separate additional charges with fiscal2025 floors, not guaranteed exact prices; the recurring trigger is each calendar year pending. Filing-fee CPI increments round down to $10; the House yearly-fee formula prints no rounding rule. Both have express no-waiver/reduction clauses.
- The pre-vote INA fee paragraph already authorizes fees. Its MAY-to-SHALL edit and deletion of cost-cap/installment/nonmandatory language are distinguished from initial authority and substantive asylum eligibility. No later fee implementation rule or PublicLaw119-21 is imported as the pre-vote baseline.
- H.Res.436/RCP119-3/adopted119-113 amendment control the May22 choice. June11H.Res.499/492 corrections and the July1EAS are separately recorded version events, not back-projected; the capturedEH is later corrected/renumbered and only the independently compared retained clauses are used here. The later Senate concurrence remains another question in this same episode without a trajectory claim.
- Employment-authorization fees/durations concern specified initial or renewed/extended documents; they do not themselves confer work permission, end TPS or grant parole. Pre-vote1158(d)(2) no-entitlement/regulation/180day condition and1254a(a) continuingTPS work authority are retained. Whole-package observations do not establish support/opposition to any fee or duration component.
- House initial and renewal/extension document limits are at most six months; Senate parole/TPS initial limits are one year or status duration, whichever shorter. Asylum-initial/renewal Senate sections do not print the House six-month sentence. Asylum-renewal House550/Senate275floors have no printed annual CPI rule; other listed EAD fees preserve their separate annual10dollar-rounded increments. Termination exceptions remain; only House prints the extra post-termination remand prohibition.
- Printed EAD allocation/antecedent issues remain application questions: House70003(a)(4) uses UNDER THIS SECTION while parole/TPS fee clauses say Treasury; Senate100010 says renewal/extension OF SUCH PAROLE in its duration sentence. Preserve the source words, not a silently resolved interpretation.
- Selected enforcement fees distinguish a prior in-absentia removal order PLUS later ICE arrest from an inadmissible person apprehended BETWEEN ports. Fiscal2025floors5000 may be higher by rule with separately printed CPI increments. Rescinded-order exception and notice/address/exceptional-circumstances/reopening-stay baseline remain. No new removal ground or actual order/arrest/collection follows from a package vote.
- House sponsor fees are separate3500and5000fiscal2025floors collected BEFOREplacement/release, not only after a child misses court;5000reimbursement is discretionary/qualified, including a rescinded-order seek-reimbursement route. Existing placement/suitability protections are retained. These conditions and fees do not supply a new suitability finding, actual court default, automatic refund or removal outcome.
- Parole-entry fees preserve all printed medical/family/transplant/adoption/temporary-return/hearing/law-enforcement predicates, not generic humanitarian labels. House Cuba-residence/family-visa/program conjunction differs from Senate granted-Cuban/Haitianentrant condition with its full definition. Exceptions and waiver bars are distinct; neither fee payment nor an exception creates parole/admission/status or an actual exemption.
- HouseSIJ500minimum is conditional on its one-viable-parent/other-nonviable predicate; SenateSIJ250minimum namesalien/parent/legalguardian and lacks that House condition/expresswaiverbar. Existing complete1101(a)(27)(J), not(a)(15)(J), supplies court/best-interest/consent/parentage qualifications; no UACage rule, duplicate-payer charges or waiver availability inferred.
- HouseTPS500additionalminimum has the exact non-admission/lapsed-nonimmigrant predicate. Senate raises existing50registrationMAXIMUMto500 and retainsreasonableMAY authority; do not substitute a universal500charge or copy the House floor/status scope. Its addedTreasury sentence coexists with an unstruck appropriation-credit baseline sentence, preserved as an application question. EADfees/status grant/duration and registration fee authority remain distinct.
- Visa-integrity reimbursement is discretionary and available only after the visa period of validity expires. House requires demonstration of one of three alternatives: no admission sought during that validity period; or compliance with all visa conditions after admission, including no unauthorized employment, together with departure no later than five days after the date authorized to remain; or filing to extend, change or adjust status within visa validity. Senate requires post-admission compliance with all visa conditions in BOTH alternatives, including no unauthorized employment, together with either (A) no request to extend the period of admission during the visa validity period AND departure no later than five days after the last day of "such period", or (B) a GRANTED nonimmigrant extension or adjustment to lawful permanent resident status during the visa validity period. The printed Senate "such period" referent remains a separate application question. Filing is not a grant; visa validity is not admission duration; the five-day reimbursement conditions do not establish general stay/work permission.
- I-94 fees attach to any-alien form application, not necessarily every entry or only land ports. The existing account deposit and appropriations refund do not create applicant refund rights. Preserve House lack of express CPI rounding versus Senate nearest-dollar increment rounding, 20-percent CBP account share and Treasury remainder separately from the visa fee.
- ESTA has separate existing $17, full-cost-recovery-with-new-$10-minimum and new-at-least-$13 components. The extended sunset concerns only clause(i)(I). Both CPI amendments name clause(i)(II) but retain broader literal prior-base references; application is reserved, with no guessed fee total or increment-rounding rule. Selected House70017 edits dispositions; selected Senate100014 does not assign new(i)(III) by name. Do not transfer House account terms or EVUS waiver language into that Senate section; other package funding coverage remains partial.
- House70018 retains commercial-aircraft/vessel passenger inspection or preinspection events. One exception requires BOTH transit to an outside-US destination and no immigration inspection. A separate exception covers immigration inspection AT DESIGNATED PORTS OF ENTRY for BOTH following arrival types: (a) a ferry meeting the retained non-ocean/non-coastwise, only-deck-passenger-and/or-vehicle, short frequent direct-route and public bridge/tunnel-service definition; or (b) Great Lakes vessels on the Great Lakes and connecting waterways WHEN OPERATING ON A REGULAR SCHEDULE. The designated-port condition applies in either arrival branch; each branch keeps its own definition/location/schedule conditions. Removing the geographical-origin exemption and replacing the separate $3 vessel charge are distinct edits. The new $1 Treasury sentence and unstruck all-(d)-receipts account baseline remain an application question, not a resolved distribution or applicant refund.
- EVUS fees apply at enrollment only to aliens subject to EVUS; neither a fee nor payment expands System eligibility or grants admission/status. House deducts $5 per enrollment, while Senate deducts $5 times payments collected; do not equate those units silently. $30 is a fiscal2025 minimum/higher-rule boundary, CPI increments round down to$0.25, waiver bars apply to EVUS and account spending permission does not prove actual expenditure.
- House70011 charges each continuance only when an alien BOTH requests it AND is granted it by an immigration judge. The separate NO-FEE exception requires a grant BASED ON statutory exceptional circumstances; it is not a waiver or any request/ordinary good cause. Circumstances must be beyond the alien's control and exclude less compelling circumstances. Examples remain illustrative: battery/extreme cruelty to the alien or the alien's child/parent; serious illness of the alien; or serious illness/death of the alien's spouse/child/parent. Each keeps its own person/event predicates; the examples are not an exclusive list. $100 is a fiscal2025 minimum or higher rule amount, not a guaranteed price; later CPI increments have no printed rounding rule.
- House70015 separately charges diversity application at filing ($400minimum/higher rule) and program registration at registration ($250minimum/higher rule). Only the application CPI increment expressly rounds down to$10; both applicable fees have waiver/reduction bars. Two separate10percent shares concern SECTION receipts for the stated fraud/cost andICE purposes; unused/uncredited amounts goTreasury without proving cash distribution. Existing allocation rules remain, and eligibility requires EITHER high-school education/equivalent OR at least two years of work experience within five years of visa application in an occupation requiring at least two years of training/experience. Work alone is not that qualified-work branch. Registration/payment neither creates the program nor guarantees selection/visa.
- EOIR70016 has TEN distinct fee events and fiscal2025 minimum/higher-rule amounts, each own annual CPI increment rounded DOWN to$10. Court application filing OR applicable prior adjudication is distinct from appeal/motion filing; no automatic double charge. Practitioner disciplinary appeals charge the filing PRACTITIONER. The bond-appeal exception and the narrow IN-ABSENTIA REOPENING motions remain separate: upon DEMONSTRATION of (lack of the specifically required notice) OR (Federal/State custody AND nonappearance through no fault), not any custody/missed hearing or all motions/reconsideration/180-day exceptional-circumstances claims. No fee or exception grants relief or rescinds an order. House(g) expressly uses the legacy SECTION AS IT EXISTED beforeApril1,1997, not a filing cutoff; House(k) no-waiver/reduction remains distinct from nonapplication exceptions. Repeated SECTION-wide50percent(a)/25percent(b)-(j) account-transfer caps are reserved for application review, not silently converted to per-fee/fixed/cumulative shares. The Legal Orientation Program OR successor restriction concerns the identified section fees used to fund those programs, not a demonstrated termination or every funding source.

- Selected exact House floor State Homeland Security Grant Program and Stonegarden funding follow. House floor 60005 common appropriation: In addition to amounts otherwise available, there is appropriated to the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency, for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury, not otherwise appropriated, to be administered under the State Homeland Security Grant Program authorized under section 2004 of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 605), to enhance State, local, and Tribal security through grants, contracts, cooperative agreements, and other activities, of which-- House floor 60005 purpose 1: $500,000,000, to remain available until September 30, 2029, for State and local capabilities to detect, identify, track, or monitor threats from unmanned aircraft systems (as such term is defined in section 44801 of title 49, United States Code); House floor 60005 purpose 2: $625,000,000, to remain available until September 30, 2029, for security, planning, and other costs related to the 2026 FIFA World Cup; House floor 60005 purpose 3: $1,000,000,000, to remain available until September 30, 2029, for security, planning, and other costs related to the 2028 Olympic Games and 2028 Paralympic Games; and House floor 60005 purpose 4: $450,000,000, to remain available until September 30, 2029, for the Operation Stonegarden Grant Program. The pre-vote fiscal year 2024 DHS/FEMA HSGP notice reproduced on Hawaii's official host describes Operation Stonegarden as supporting enhanced cooperation and coordination among CBP, USBP, and Federal, State, local, Tribal and territorial law enforcement agencies to improve overall border security. It funds joint border-security efforts along routes of ingress and egress to and from international borders, including travel corridors in States bordering Mexico and Canada and States and territories with international water borders. In that notice, those State, local, Tribal and territorial law enforcement agencies use their inherent law enforcement authorities and receive no additional authority from participating in Stonegarden. This is dated program-purpose context, not a new power conferred by the House appropriation or a complete 2025 eligibility rule. The floor clause appropriates to the FEMA Administrator additional fiscal year 2025 funds administered under the State Homeland Security Grant Program in 6 U.S.C. 605 for State/local/Tribal security through the printed grant, contract, cooperative-agreement and other activity paths. Each of its four purpose amounts has its own availability until September 30, 2029. The Stonegarden amount is $450,000,000. House FIFA purpose (2) expressly includes planning; House purpose (3) expressly names the 2028 Olympic Games and 2028 Paralympic Games. The Senate prints different event wording; no decision about either version's actual event-expense eligibility is inferred. The House selected text prints no Senate 90005(a)(2) FIFA/Olympics exemption or added consistent-with-titles-18-and-49 phrase. - Selected exact House 110019 death/disability loan-discharge income-exclusion and SSN provisions follow. House 110019 exclusion grounds: In the case of an individual, gross income does not include any amount which (but for this subsection) would be includible in gross income for such taxable year by reason of the discharge (in whole or in part) of any loan described in subparagraph (B), if such discharge was-- (i) pursuant to subsection (a) or (d) of section 437 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 or the parallel benefit under part D of title IV of such Act (relating to the repayment of loan liability), (ii) pursuant to section 464(c)(1)(F) of such Act, or (iii) otherwise discharged on account of death or total and permanent disability of the student. House 110019 loan categories: A loan is described in this subparagraph if such loan is-- (i) a student loan (as defined in paragraph (2)), or (ii) a private education loan (as defined in section 140(a) of the Consumer Credit Protection Act (15 U.S.C. 1650(a)). House 110019 identification and own marital rules: (i) In general.--Subparagraph (A) shall not apply with respect to any discharge during any taxable year unless the taxpayer includes on the return of tax for such taxable year-- (I) the taxpayer's social security number, and (II) if the taxpayer is married, the social security number of such taxpayers's spouse. (ii) Social security number.--For purposes of this subparagraph, the term `social security number' has the meaning given such term in section 24(h)(7). (iii) Married individuals.--Rules similar to the rules of section 32(d) shall apply to this subparagraph.. House 110019 math-error amendment: Section 6213(g)(2) is amended by striking and at the end of subparagraph (U), by striking the period at the end of subparagraph (V) and inserting , and, and by inserting after subparagraph (V) the following new subparagraph: (W) an omission of a correct social security number required under section 108(f)(5)(C) (relating to discharges on account of death or disability).. House 110019 discharge-date applicability: The amendments made by this section shall apply to discharges after December 31, 2025. Each version replaces only 108(f)(5) with the printed exclusion, not all of section 108 or every student-loan tax rule. The original 2024 (5) instead covers its defined discharge categories after December 31, 2020 and before January 1, 2026; the candidate does not silently extend that entire temporary rule unchanged. The common requirement that the discharged loan meet new subparagraph (B) applies across all three ground alternatives. This does not mean every education-related debt qualifies. A parent borrower is not silently equated to the student. Full 437(a) retains qualifying loans, death/disability determinations, safeguards, conditional reinstatement, VA documentation and own income-monitoring/approval/opt-out/update rules; 437(d) separately addresses a parent loan when the student dies. Captured 464(c)(1)(F) retains loan-fund agreement scope, borrower death, regulated permanent/total disability, the medically determinable substantial-gainful-activity alternative with its own duration/death tests, and VA unemployability due to service-connected disability. Part D parallel benefit is retained with complete captured 455 and its unless-otherwise-specified limitation, not a universal cancellation promise. Tax exclusion after a qualifying discharge is distinct from authority to cancel a loan. Both versions define the SSN by 24(h)(7), with their own same-bill amended definition and previously bound SSA issuance authority: citizen or the specified authorization route, and issuance before the return due date, not a bare identification number or a citizen-only rule. - Selected exact House account and separate pilot eligibility clauses follow. House 110115 account establishment and instrument: The term `TRUMP account' means a trust created or organized in the United States for the exclusive benefit of an individual and which is designated (in such manner as the Secretary shall prescribe) at the time of the establishment of the trust as a TRUMP account, but only if the written governing instrument creating the trust meets the following requirements: (A) The individual establishing the account shall provide to the trustee the social security number of such individual and of the account beneficiary. (B) Except in the case of a qualified rollover contribution described in subsection (e), no contribution will be accepted-- (i) before January 1, 2026, (ii) unless it is in cash, (iii) unless the account beneficiary has not attained age 18, and (iv) if such contribution would result in aggregate contributions for the taxable year exceeding the contribution limit specified in subsection (c)(1). (C) No distribution (other than a distribution of a qualified rollover contribution) will be allowed-- (i) before the date on which the account beneficiary attains age 18, or (ii) in the case of such an account the account beneficiary of which has not attained age 25, if the aggregate distributions from such account exceeds the amount that is \1/2\ the cash equivalent value of the account on the date on which the account beneficiary attains age 18. (D) The account beneficiary has not attained age 8 on the date of the establishment of the account. (E) The trustee is a bank (as defined in section 408(n)) or another person who demonstrates to the satisfaction of the Secretary that the manner in which that person will administer the trust will be consistent with the requirements of this section or who has so demonstrated with respect to any individual retirement plan. (F) The interest of an individual in the balance of his account is nonforfeitable. (G) The assets of the trust shall not be commingled with other property except in a common trust fund or common investment fund. (H) No part of the trust funds will be invested in any asset other than eligible investments. House 110115 account beneficiary: The term `account beneficiary' means the individual on whose behalf the TRUMP account was established. House 110115 tax-year applicability: The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024. House 110116 one-time credit and account-only payment: In the case of any taxpayer with respect to whom an eligible individual is a qualifying child, there shall be allowed a one-time credit of $1,000 with respect to each such eligible individual who is a qualifying child of such taxpayer which shall be payable by the Secretary only to the TRUMP account with respect to which such eligible individual is the account beneficiary. House 110116 Secretary account establishment and opt-out: (1) In general.--In the case of any eligible individual that the Secretary determines is not the account beneficiary of any TRUMP account as of the qualifying date of such eligible individual, the Secretary shall establish an account for the benefit of such eligible individual. (2) Qualifying date.--For purposes of paragraph (1), the term `qualifying date' means, with respect to an eligible individual, the first date on which a return of tax is filed by an individual with respect to whom such eligible individual is a qualifying child with respect to the taxable year to which such return relates. (3) Notification.--In the case of any eligible individual for the benefit of whom the Secretary establishes an account under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall-- (A) notify any individual with respect to whom such eligible individual is a qualifying child for the taxable year described in paragraph (2) of the establishment of such account, and (B) shall provide an opportunity to such individual to elect to decline the application of this subsection to such qualifying child. (4) Determination of default trustee.--For purposes of selecting a trustee for an account established under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall take into account-- (A) the history of reliability and regulatory compliance of such trustee, (B) the customer service experience of such trustee, (C) the costs imposed by such trustee on the account or account beneficiary, and (D) to the extent practicable, the preferences of any individual described in paragraph (3)(A) with respect to such eligible individual. House 110116 pilot birth window and citizenship at birth: For purposes of subsection (a), the term eligible individual means an individual-- (1) who is born after December 31, 2024, and before January 1, 2029, and (2) who is a United States citizen at birth. House 110116 pilot return identification: (1) In general.--No credit shall be allowed under subsection (a) to a taxpayer unless such taxpayer includes on the return of tax for the taxable year-- (A) such individual's social security number, (B) if such individual is married, the social security number of such individual's spouse, and (C) the social security number of the eligible individual with respect to whom such credit is allowed. (2) Social security number defined.--For purposes of paragraph (1), the term `social security number' shall have the meaning given such term in section 24(h)(7). House 110116 pilot definitions: For purposes of this section-- (1) Qualifying child.--The term qualifying child has the meaning given such term in section 152(c). (2) TRUMP account; account beneficiary.--The terms `TRUMP account' and `account beneficiary' have the meaning given such terms in section 530A(b).. House 110116 improper-claim penalty and incorporated definitions: In the case of any taxpayer that makes an excessive claim for a credit under section 6434-- (1) if such excess is a result of negligence or disregard of the rules or regulations, there shall be imposed a penalty of $500, or (2) if such excess is a result of fraud, there shall be imposed a penalty of $1,000. (b) Definitions.--The terms `negligence' and `disregard' have the same meaning as when such terms are used in section 6662.. House 110116 math-error amendment: Section 6213(g)(2), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, is amended by striking and at the end of subparagraph (Y), by striking the period at the end of subparagraph (Z) and inserting , and, and by inserting after subparagraph (Z) the following new subparagraph: (AA) an omission of a correct social security number required under section 6434(d)(1) (relating to the TRUMP accounts contribution pilot program).. House 110116 tax-year applicability: The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024. Account creation and pilot contribution eligibility are separate. The account-only clauses above do not print the pilot citizenship test, and the candidate does not import that test to every account. Nor does a trust organized in the United States establish the birthplace or citizenship of an account beneficiary. Each pilot retains its own birth window after December 31, 2024 and before January 1, 2029, qualifying-child reference and account-only payment; a birth window does not mean a United States birthplace. Complete original 152 definitions, exceptions, qualifying-child relationship, residence, age, self-support and joint-return conditions, tie-breakers, divorced-parent alternatives, adoption/foster-child definitions and limited missing-child rule are bound. No automatic parent claim, universal child entitlement or taxpayer citizenship classification is inferred. The defined-number references use their own same-bill 24(h)(7) and complete SSA issuance route, citizen or specified authorization, with each applicable issuance deadline retained. Number validity is distinct from citizenship and from all remaining eligibility requirements. No child-credit amount or earlier loan-exclusion similar-32(d) marital clause is imported into the pilot. Existing notice, 60-day conditional abatement-request and deficiency context remains separate from the new math-error list addition. The new fixed-dollar negligence/fraud alternatives incorporate only 6662 definitions, not its 20-percent penalty; no actual negligence, fraud, assessment or payment is inferred. General retirement/investment/distribution/employer-contribution and unrelated tax mechanics outside the selected clauses remain bound section context, not fully interpreted component claims. Other H.R.1 components and separately reserved application questions remain unfinished. House account instrument requires the establishing individual and beneficiary SSNs, without an explicit 24(h)(7) definition in that account-only clause. It separately requires a beneficiary under age 8 at establishment; its non-rollover contribution restrictions retain January 1, 2026, cash, under-18 and contribution-limit conditions, and its distribution rule retains age-18 birthday and under-25 half-value conditions. The pilot separately requires citizenship at birth, taxpayer and eligible-individual SSNs on the return and a spouse SSN if the individual is married; it does not add a similar-32(d) rule. Secretary establishment follows the exact no-account determination at the first qualifying return, with notification and an opportunity to decline, not unconditional enrollment of every child. Account and pilot tax-year applicability after December 31, 2024 is distinct from the account contribution-start date. - Selected exact House tips and overtime deduction/identification clauses follow. House 110101 deduction and reporting gate: There shall be allowed as a deduction an amount equal to the qualified tips received during the taxable year that are included on statements furnished to the individual pursuant to section 6041(d)(3), 6041A(e)(3), 6050W(f)(2), 6051(a)(18), or reported by the taxpayer on Form 4137 (or successor). House 110101 business receipt/expense limit: In the case of qualified tips received by an individual during any taxable year in the course of any trade or business of such individual, such qualified tips shall be taken into account under subsection (a) only to the extent that the gross receipts of the taxpayer from such trade or business for such taxable year (including such qualified tips) exceeds the sum of-- (1) cost of goods sold that are allocable to such receipts, plus (2) other expenses, losses, or deductions (other than the deduction allowed under this section), which are properly allocable to such receipts. House 110101 qualified-tip conditions: For purposes of this section-- (1) In general.--The term `qualified tip' means any cash tip received by an individual in an occupation which traditionally and customarily received tips on or before December 31, 2024, as provided by the Secretary. (2) Exclusions.--Such term shall not include any amount received by an individual unless-- (A) such amount is paid voluntarily without any consequence in the event of nonpayment, is not the subject of negotiation, and is determined by the payor, (B) the trade or business in the course of which the individual receives such amount is not a specified service trade or business (as defined in section 199A(d)(2)), (C) such individual does not receive earned income (within the meaning of section 32) in excess of the dollar amount in effect under section 414(q)(1)(B)(i) for the calendar year in which the taxable year begins, and (D) such other requirements as may be established by the Secretary in regulations or other guidance are satisfied. House 110101 identification and own marital rules: (1) In general.--No deduction shall be allowed under this section unless the taxpayer includes on the return of tax for the taxable year-- (A) such individual's social security number, and (B) if the individual is married, the social security number of such individual's spouse. (2) Married individuals.--Rules similar to the rules of section 32(d) shall apply to this section. (3) Social security number defined.--For purposes of paragraph (1), the term `social security number' shall have the meaning given such term in section 24(h)(7).. House 110101 anti-reclassification regulations: The Secretary shall prescribe such regulations or other guidance as may be necessary to prevent reclassification of income as qualified tips, including regulations or other guidance to prevent abuse of the deduction allowed by this section. House 110101 deduction termination: No deduction shall be allowed under this section for any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2028.. [[Page H2301]] House 110101 non-itemizer deduction: Section 63(b) is amended by striking and at the end of paragraph (3), by striking the period at the end of paragraph (4) and inserting and, and by adding at the end the following new paragraph: (5) the deduction provided in section 224.. House 110101 math-error amendment: Section 6213(g)(2), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, is amended by striking and at the end of subparagraph (V), by striking the period at the end of subparagraph (W) and inserting , and, and by inserting after subparagraph (W) the following new subparagraph: (X) an omission of a correct social security number required under section 224(d) (relating to deduction for qualified tips).. House 110101 tax-year applicability: The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024. House 110102 deduction: There shall be allowed as a deduction an amount equal to the qualified overtime compensation received during the taxable year. House 110102 qualified-overtime conditions: (1) In general.--For purposes of this section, the term `qualified overtime compensation' means overtime compensation paid to an individual required under section 7 of the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 that is in excess of the regular rate (as used in such section) at which such individual is employed. (2) Exclusions.--Such term shall not include-- (A) any qualified tip (as defined in section 224(c)), or (B) any amount received by an individual during a taxable year if such individual is a highly compensated employee (as defined in section 414(q)(1)) of any employer for the calendar year in which the taxable year begins, or receives earned income in excess of the dollar amount in effect under section 414(q)(1)(B)(i) for such calendar year. House 110102 identification and own marital rules: (1) In general.--No deduction shall be allowed under this section unless the taxpayer includes on the return of tax for the taxable year-- (A) such individual's social security number, and (B) if the individual is married, the social security number of such individual's spouse. (2) Married individuals.--Rules similar to the rules of section 32(d) shall apply to this section. (3) Social security number defined.--For purposes of paragraph (1), the term `social security number' shall have the meaning given such term in section 24(h)(7).. House 110102 regulations: The Secretary shall issue such regulations or other guidance as may be necessary or appropriate to carry out the purposes of this section. House 110102 deduction termination: No deduction shall be allowed under this section for any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2028.. House 110102 non-itemizer deduction: Section 63(b), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, is amended by striking and at the end of paragraph (4), by striking the period at the end of paragraph (5) and inserting and, and by adding at the end the following new paragraph: (6) the deduction provided in section 225.. House 110102 math-error amendment: Section 6213(g)(2), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, is amended by striking and at the end of subparagraph (W), by striking the period at the end of subparagraph (X) and inserting , and, and by inserting after subparagraph (X) the following new subparagraph: (Y) an omission of a correct social security number required under section 225(c) (relating to deduction for qualified overtime).. House 110102 tax-year applicability: The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024. These provisions allow deductions for their own qualified income, not exemption of every dollar described colloquially as tips or overtime and not a guarantee of zero tax. Each retains the complete printed qualified-income gates and its own new statutory subsection references; statements/Form 4137 references, business net-income limits, exceptions and regulatory instructions are not omitted. The original 199A(d)(2) service-business definition is bound with its own 1202/475 references, without importing the separate 199A(d)(3) qualified-business-income phase-in as an automatic tips exception or classifying an actual profession. Overtime means compensation required under FLSA section 7 in excess of the regular rate, not all compensation for hours described as overtime or a taxpayer employment determination. Complete original section 7 with common applicability, regular-rate inclusions/exclusions, alternative arrangements, compensatory-time and other own limitations is bound; no universal 40-hour or all-worker eligibility claim is inferred. Other financial/reporting context remains in complete source bindings without an actual implementation conclusion. Other H.R.1 components and separately reserved questions remain unfinished. House tips and overtime require taxpayer SSN and a spouse SSN if married, plus rules similar to 32(d). Full joint-return default and separated-spouse exception retain qualifying-child residence and alternative abode/decree/household conjunctions; actual adaptation to these deductions is reserved as question 58, not a universal child/joint-return requirement. Full original 414(q) definition, its preceding-year/employer-election/ownership/adjustment/coordination and nonresident-alien context, plus 32(c)(2) earned-income definition and exclusions are bound. No fixed unadjusted $80,000 threshold or actual employee/income classification is inferred.
