- Selected Senate 71301/71302/71303 retain own eligible-alien/income/verification predicates and effective dates; these sections do not contain House named-memo amendments. No House title-wide/CSR-section/Federal-payment-sentence exclusion is imported, and no automatic DACA eligibility or whole-package absence of DACA effects is inferred. Original memo is historical context, not a current ACA eligibility decision.
- The qualifying child's defined SSN is required in either case. The Senate also requires the taxpayer's defined SSN or, on a joint return, the defined SSN of at least one spouse. This is not both spouses on every joint return or a child number alone. No House SIMILAR 32(d) is imported. Own $2,200 context and after-2025 credit inflation; The senior mechanism in 70103 is addressed separately below. Both child-credit amendments begin with TAXABLE YEARS BEGINNING AFTER DECEMBER 31, 2024. The defined SSN may be issued to either a US citizen or an individual under the named work-authorized-alien branch. In either case, it must have been issued before the due date for the return. Any SSA number, an ITIN or citizenship proof alone is insufficient. Complete 24/152 retain own qualifying-child, NOT-ATTAINED-17, citizenship/residence/adoption, relationship/support/abode/joint-return/tie/custody and other exceptions, income/refundable/identification/year limits. Existing 24(h)(4)(C) PARAGRAPH (7) fallback is RETAINED but new claimant/spouse-failure application RESERVED as question 39: no guaranteed $500 or whole-family loss. Zero-exemption reference rule does not itself eliminate credit. Mathematical-error scope changes to SECTION 24; own alleged-error/explanation notice, no petition BASED ON THAT NOTICE, abatement request WITHIN 60 DAYS AFTER NOTICE SENT, mandatory abatement UPON RECEIPT, deficiency reassessment and collection stay remain. No actual fraud, debt, indexed payment, credit/refund, every-remedy loss or individual/tax-family determination.
- The Senate $6,000 deduction is per qualified person. The listed alternatives are the taxpayer or the spouse on a joint return. In either case, the claimed person must have attained 65 before the tax year closes and must supply that person's defined SSN. One spouse's number does not establish deductions for both. The phaseout rate is 6 percent over $75,000, or $150,000 on a joint return. A taxpayer married within section 7703 must file jointly with the spouse; the new House similar-32(d) clause, blind bonus and hypothetical-itemizer mechanism are not imported. Own mathematical-error label is (W). The same-version SSN definition permits issuance to either a US citizen or the named work-authorized-alien category. In either case, the number must have been issued before the due date for the return. Other SSA numbers or ITINs do not alone qualify. Child-credit identification is not senior identification. Own taxable-income, itemization, spouse/exemption and marital predicates remain, along with the nonresident-alien standard-deduction exclusion, without an individual eligibility finding or accepted override. A deduction is not a dollar-for-dollar credit, exemption of all Social Security income or guaranteed refund. Both senior amendments apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024; their own upper limit is a taxable year beginning before January 1, 2029. Modified income includes the named 911/931/933 exclusions. Mathematical-error notice requires the alleged error and explanation; the no-petition rule concerns that notice. The abatement request period is 60 days after notice is sent, abatement follows receipt, reassessment uses deficiency procedures and collection is stayed during the abatement period. No actual debt, fraud, payment or loss of every remedy.
- Senate requires the individual's defined SSN in all cases. A credit for the qualified expenses of an individual other than the taxpayer or spouse must also include that individual's name and defined SSN. No new House spouse-number or similar-32(d) amendment is imported; retained 25A(g)(6) requires joint filing for a taxpayer married within 7703. No separate-return eligibility or child-credit joint-number alternative is inferred. The same-version defined SSN permits citizen issuance or the named work-authorized-alien branch. In either case, issuance must precede the return due date; an ITIN or any SSA number does not alone suffice. The old AOTC student on-or-before deadline is distinct. The institution EIN clause is AOTC-only and tied to the named taxpayer-paid qualified expenses taken into account, with retained dependent-payment treatment; it is not a Lifetime Learning or every-institution requirement. Full credit, income, student, institution, qualified-expense, assistance, dependent, prepayment, double-benefit, payee-statement, refund and recapture conditions remain, without an individual amount or eligibility determination. The AOTC student reference freezes HEA 484(a)(1), with its own exceptions, at August 5, 1997; it does not import all current student eligibility or its citizenship paragraph. The institution definition retains frozen HEA 481 and its own title IV eligibility condition. Exact historical passages and amendment chronology are bound; full HEA 481 comparison uses two declared split-word normalizations, without source mutation or personal/institution classification. A taxpayer nonresident during any portion of the year retains the conditional 6013(g)/(h) chapter-1 resident-election path, each with own spouse/status/both-election and duration/termination/re-election predicates; this is not all-noncitizen denial or immigration status/work authorization. Both apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025. Own mathematical-error (J) changes TIN to SSN or EIN; alleged-error/explanation notice, 60 days after notice is sent, abatement upon receipt, deficiency reassessment and collection stay remain. No debt, wrongdoing, guaranteed credit/refund, loss of every remedy or whole-package closure.
- Senate 100052(8) family-unity funding uses a purpose within the $29.85 billion additional fiscal year 2025 ICE account, available through September 30, 2029; neither the full envelope nor House $20 million is a separate Senate family earmark. Pending specified charge, charged only with the INA 275(a) misdemeanor and entry with the alien's under-18 child all retain their own scope; care/custody expressly in accordance with applicable laws, plus co-detention purpose. Charge is not guilt or an actual custody result. Accompanied parent/child is not UAC; no House child-disclosure/withdrawal mechanism, universal detention or family entitlement imported. No individual outcome, legal-constraint adjudication or full-package closure.
- Senate 100052 uses one additional fiscal year 2025 $29.85 billion ICE envelope through September 30, 2029 for listed purposes; no House account amounts or hiring minima imported. Hiring/training includes named investigators and retired hiring priority; recruitment/onboarding distinct. The Director may provide a performance bonus to a named ICE agent, officer or attorney who demonstrates exemplary service. The Director may provide a retention bonus to a named ICE agent, officer or attorney who commits to two additional years of immigration-enforcement service. The Director may provide a signing bonus to a named ICE agent, officer or attorney only if that person is hired on or after enactment and commits to five years of immigration-enforcement service. Signing is may, unlike House shall. For retention and signing bonuses, the Director shall provide each qualifying individual a written service agreement with its required period, amount, payment and early-termination terms. Transportation/related departure-removal costs, IT including fee collection, facilities/fleet, 287(g) agreements, VOICE staffing/nonfinancial victim assistance and OPLA immigration-enforcement/removal representation remain distinct purposes. Full material 287(g) limits, State/local expense and voluntary agreement/own no-agreement communication/cooperation paths remain; no blanket deputization, power or immunity. Victim-assistance perpetrator condition is not status-based guilt, cash for every victim or actual crime. Family paragraph (8) remains separately qualified. No actual hiring/bonus/agreement/collection/removal/expenditure or full-package closure.
- Senate 90002 provides $4.1 billion for personnel, $2,052,630,000 for bonuses/awards and $855 million for vehicles. Each of those three paragraphs is a fiscal year 2025 appropriation expressly available until September 30, 2029. The separate $5 billion for facilities and checkpoints owned, leased or operated by CBP does not print that phrase, with availability application reserved as question 45 before any borrowed or assumed expiry. Coordinator recruiting/hiring/training restriction applies to (a) funds after October 31, 2028, not immediate/all-funding employment prohibition. Own recruitment/performance/retention and repair/unit purposes, no House/ICE substitution. 90004 $6.168 billion envelope until September 30, 2029 includes its own listed technology/entry-or-exit/initial-UAC-screening/trafficking/commemoration purposes, not separate House earmarks. Southwest/northern tower condition requires same tower both tested and accepted by CBP under own autonomous definition; fund/geographic/authority scope distinct, no actual accuracy or immigration finding. Complete biometric/UAC/TVPRA conditions retained, no every-traveller collection or imported House tattoo/disclosure/withdrawal mechanism. 90007 DHS $10 billion border-support cost reimbursement has own dates/purpose, not an inferred State-only/January-date restriction or actual award. 100053 provides a $750 million FLETC envelope, with at least $285 million for training and at most $465 million for facilities. Training includes newly hired Federal law enforcement personnel employed by DHS and State and local law enforcement agencies operating in support of DHS. Facility purposes include the named maintenance and training equipment. These are not exact House splits. Own stated availability until September 30, 2029 retained. No individual enforcement/child outcome, actual hire/award/data/reimbursement/expenditure or full-package closure.
- Senate 100054 fiscal year 2025 $3.33 billion DOJ envelope through September 30, 2029 has separate selected EOIR, Byrne/COPS and incarceration purposes; neither all funds nor House earmarks are assigned to one. EOIR judges/support addresses backlog; not-more-than-800-judges ceiling effective November 1, 2028 is not an actual count, minimum or inferred cut. Paragraph (7) compensation requires felony or at least two misdemeanor convictions in every case, plus one complete entry/proceeding-at-custody/nonimmigrant-status-failure-at-custody alternative, with all listed entity funding exclusions retained. No status/charge shortcut, actual award or State violation. Paragraph (5) located community-violence funding limitation and AG-determined 1373 compliance, and (7)(C) more-than-one-State distribution, print under-this-subsection references with scope reserved as question 46; no settled whole-account or purpose-only application. Complete 1373 own information-purpose/agency boundaries and old 241(i) compensation route retained, not constitutional acceptance, unlimited data/arrest authority, first-ever compensation, or imported old-route conditions. No individual guilt/State disqualification/actual hires/backlog/grant/custody/removal outcome or full-package closure.
- Senate 100054(2)/(3) drug/prosecution purposes use the shared $3.33 billion fiscal year 2025 envelope through September 30, 2029, without House earmarks. Own listed matters include unlawful voting; full 611 federal-office/exception/nonapplication predicates remain, no generic alien-guilt or new benefit/voting rule. Separate 100055 DOJ Fund. The Attorney General shall use the Fund amounts for grants to eligible States, State agencies, and units of local government, pursuant to their existing statutory authorities, for any of the following purposes. The paragraph 1 purpose is locating and apprehending aliens who have committed a crime under Federal, State, or local law, in addition to being unlawfully present in the United States. The paragraph 2 purpose is collection and analysis of law enforcement investigative information within the United States to counter gang or other criminal activity. The paragraph 3 purpose is investigating and prosecuting crimes committed by aliens within the United States and drug and human trafficking crimes committed within the United States. The paragraph 4 purpose is court operations related to the prosecution of crimes committed by aliens and drug and human trafficking crimes. The paragraph 5 purpose is temporary criminal detention of aliens. The paragraph 6 purpose is transporting aliens described in paragraph (1) within the United States to locations related to the apprehension, detention, and prosecution of such aliens. The paragraph 7 purpose is vehicle maintenance, logistics, transportation, and other support provided to law enforcement agencies by a State agency to enhance the ability to locate and apprehend aliens who have committed crimes under Federal, State, or local law, in addition to being unlawfully present in the United States. Paragraphs (1) and (7) retain their own additional-crime and unlawful-presence requirements; paragraph (6) retains the paragraph (1) person category, its domestic transport limit and its destination purposes. Those requirements are not imported into the other purposes. Temporary criminal detention is distinct from civil immigration detention. Court paragraph (4) prints no separate within-the-United-States phrase; no neighboring location condition is borrowed. Listed conjunctions report the source categories, not a determination that a particular grant must fund both crime categories. Existing statutory authorities do not create new State arrest/removal powers or establish actual crime/status/expense eligibility. Fiscal year 2025 appropriation is not to exceed $3,500,000,000 ($3.5 billion) until September 30, 2028, with qualified and documented expenses. The Attorney General may provide grants to State agencies and units of local government for their expenditures for completed, ongoing, or new activities determined to be eligible for such grant funding that occurred on or after January 20, 2021. Amounts made available under this section shall be distributed to more than 1 State. No borrowed January 21 or 2029 date, automatic grant, actual crime/status/detention/hiring/spending or full-package closure. Existing question 46 subsection-scope application is unchanged.
- Senate 100051(9)/(10) use the additional fiscal year 2025 $2,055,000,000 DHS envelope through September 30, 2029, in accordance with 235(b)(1)/(c), without House earmarks, House's express 212(a)(2)/(3) grounds wording or regardless-of-presence phrase. Complete own screening/designation/asylum/fear/record/requested-review/consultation/detention/exception/protected-status procedures remain. Both AG confidential-information inadmissibility and post-consultation disclosure-prejudice predicates precede discretionary 235(c) removal without further immigration-judge inquiry; further-inquiry and written-submission rules remain. Full criminal/security grounds and conditional waivers are not conviction-only or automatic status classifiers. Full 242(e) limited judicial-review/relief/court/deadline/remedy/inquiry scope and distinct January 2025 State-enforcement/injunction amendments retained. Questions 47/48 stay House application reservations, not new Senate expansion rules. No actual crime/status/waiver/asylum/hearing/review/custody/removal or full-package closure.
- Senate 100051(8) and (11) are purposes within the additional $2,055,000,000 fiscal year 2025 appropriation to the Secretary of Homeland Security, available through September 30, 2029. Neither purpose is a separate earmark for the full account, the ICE account or a House child appropriation. Paragraph (8) funds removal operations for specified unaccompanied alien children, but amounts under this paragraph shall only be used for permitting a specified unaccompanied alien child to withdraw the application for admission of the child pursuant to section 235(a)(4). The Secretary of Homeland Security must determine on a case-by-case basis all three specified-child conditions. First, the child has been found by an immigration officer at a land border or port of entry of the United States and is inadmissible under the Immigration and Nationality Act. Second, the child has not been a victim of severe forms of trafficking in persons, and there is no credible evidence that such child is at risk of being trafficked upon return of the child to the child's country of nationality or country of last habitual residence. Third, the child does not have a fear of returning to the child's country of nationality or country of last habitual residence owing to a credible fear of persecution. The paragraph does not print the House express contiguous-or-non-contiguous-country phrase or an independent-decision finding; neither is silently inserted into its definition. The incorporated unaccompanied-alien-child definition requires no lawful immigration status in the United States and not having attained 18 years of age, together with either no parent or legal guardian in the United States or no parent or legal guardian in the United States available to provide care and physical custody. The complete severe-forms-of-trafficking definition is bound with its own sex-trafficking and labor-or-services alternatives, force/fraud/coercion and under-18 distinctions; no label alone determines a child's eligibility. Paragraph (11) funds criminal and gang checks of defined unaccompanied alien children who are 12 years of age and older, including the examination of such unaccompanied alien children for gang-related tattoos and other gang-related markings. It prints no separate encountered-by-CBP condition; the House 70116 encounter condition is not imported. Its age-12 floor belongs to this check purpose, not the paragraph (8) withdrawal definition. Examination funding is not a finding that a child belongs to a gang, has committed a crime or is dangerous. Complete material captured pre-vote 235(a)(4) retains discretionary permission to withdraw and depart immediately, not a mandatory withdrawal or removal order. Complete TVPRA 235/1232 retains its own contiguous-child case-by-case trafficking/fear and independent-decision conditions, discretionary withdrawal/return, safe-return conditions, 48-hour screening and failed-or-undetermined-screen transfer, other-child custody pathway and own notification/72-hour-transfer exceptions. Its removal-proceedings, relief/access-to-counsel, placement, suitability and remaining safeguards retain their own scope. Senate funding does not itself establish their repeal, fulfillment or a universal individual return, protection or counsel outcome. Exact application interaction remains separate question 49; House question 43 is preserved independently.
- Senate 100051(5) fingerprint and DNA purposes are within the additional $2,055,000,000 fiscal year 2025 Secretary of Homeland Security account through September 30, 2029. Both purposes share the printed circumstance of aliens and alien children entering the United States without a valid visa. Subparagraph (A) funds collecting fingerprints, in accordance with section 262 and subsections (a)(3) and (b) of section 235 of the Immigration and Nationality Act. Subparagraph (B) separately funds collecting DNA, in accordance with sections 235(d) and 287(b) of that Act. These are funding purposes with their own incorporated authorities, not a determination that every alien or child is subject to every collection power or that funded collection actually occurred. Captured 262(a) concerns an alien now or hereafter in the United States who is fourteen years of age or older, has not been registered and fingerprinted under section 1201(b) or section 30 or 31 of the Alien Registration Act, 1940, and remains in the United States for thirty days or longer. All those conditions are common to its duty to apply for registration and to be fingerprinted before the expiration of such thirty days. Captured 262(b) separately requires a parent or legal guardian to apply for registration of an alien now or hereafter in the United States who is less than fourteen years of age, has not been registered under those named provisions, and remains in the United States for thirty days or longer, before that period expires. That parent/guardian provision prints registration, not the same under-14 fingerprint duty. Whenever an alien attains his fourteenth birthday in the United States, the separate rule requires in-person registration and fingerprinting within thirty days thereafter. Captured 262(c) retains the Attorney General's discretionary nonimmigrant fingerprint waiver on the basis of reciprocity pursuant to prescribed regulations; no actual waiver is inferred. Complete 235(a)(3) concerns inspection of aliens, including crewmen, who apply for or otherwise seek admission, readmission or transit; it does not itself print a fingerprint command. Complete material 235(b)(1)/(2) screening, exceptions, asylum/fear/interview/review/consultation/detention and contiguous-return conditions remain bound, together with the original favorable-admission challenge. January 29, 2025 Public Law 119-1 renumbers that original challenge from (3) to (4) and inserts the distinct State enforcement (3); the captured 2024 wording is not relabeled as an unamended 2025 subsection. Complete 235(d) retains its own belief-based conveyance search, detention/delivery with the alien-crewmember exception, named oath/evidence powers and subpoena-purpose/court-enforcement conditions. Complete 287(b) retains the designated officer/employee oath/evidence scope and its own knowing-or-willful false-evidence/perjury conditions. Neither cited provision expressly names DNA collection. That literal observation does not resolve whether other law, implementation rules or this funding language supports a proposed collection; question 50 reserves the exact DNA authority/application interaction. Question 51 separately reserves the fingerprint-purpose no-valid-visa circumstance alongside the incorporated registration age/prior-registration/duration/waiver paths and inspection procedures. No statutory repeal, guaranteed discretion outcome, universal biometric collection or actual child/parent/status/registration finding is inferred.
- Remaining Senate 100051 purposes (1) through (4), (6), (7) and (12) share the additional $2,055,000,000 fiscal year 2025 appropriation to the Secretary of Homeland Security, available through September 30, 2029. They are purposes within that account, not separate full-envelope earmarks or borrowed ICE/House amounts. The paragraph 1 purpose is hiring and training of additional U.S. Customs and Border Protection agents, and the necessary support staff, to carry out immigration enforcement activities. The paragraph 2 purpose is funding for transportation costs and related costs associated with the departure or removal of aliens. The paragraph 3 purpose is funding for the assignment of Department of Homeland Security employees and State officers to carry out immigration enforcement activities pursuant to sections 103(a) and 287(g) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1103(a) and 1357(g)). The paragraph 4 purpose is hiring additional staff and investing the necessary resources to enhance screening and vetting of all aliens seeking entry into United States, consistent with section 212 of such Act (8 U.S.C. 1182), or intending to remain in the United States, consistent with section 237 of such Act (8 U.S.C. 1227). The paragraph 6 purpose is transporting and facilitating the return, pursuant to section 235(b)(2)(C) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1225(b)(2)(C)), of aliens arriving from contiguous territory. The paragraph 7 purpose is funding for State and local participation in homeland security efforts for purposes of: ending the presence of criminal gangs and criminal organizations throughout the United States; addressing crime and public safety threats; combating human smuggling and trafficking networks throughout the United States; supporting immigration enforcement activities; and providing reimbursement for State and local participation in such efforts. The paragraph 12 purpose is information technology investments to support immigration purposes, including improvements to fee and revenue collections. The entry and intended-remain screening categories retain their own section 212 and section 237 references. The State/local participation list retains all five own purposes, including its own throughout-the-United-States phrases. It does not borrow the reimbursement fund's crime-plus-unlawful-presence category or domestic transport restriction. The general departure/removal transportation purpose prints no separate within-the-United-States phrase. The assignment list retains Department of Homeland Security employees and State officers pursuant to both printed statutory references, not authority for any State employee to exercise all Federal powers. The printed purpose lists do not determine that a particular expenditure must fulfill every listed category. Fee and revenue collection IT is not a new fee, fine or penalty charge. Complete captured 103(a) retains its named agency roles, regulatory/delegation powers, consents and other conditions. In captured 103(a)(10), the Attorney General may authorize a State or local law enforcement officer to perform or exercise any of the powers, privileges, or duties conferred or imposed by this chapter or regulations issued thereunder upon officers or employees of the Service only in the event of the Attorney General's determination that an actual or imminent mass influx of aliens arriving off the coast of the United States, or near a land border, presents urgent circumstances requiring an immediate Federal response, and with the consent of the head of the department, agency, or establishment under whose jurisdiction the individual is serving. The captured event-specific authorization does not establish general unconditioned State power. Previously bound full 287(g) agreement qualifications, training, written powers/duration, Federal direction/supervision, voluntary/communication/cooperation and expense/employment/liability distinctions remain unchanged. Complete captured section 212(a) grounds and remaining operative section 212 authorities retain their own standards, exceptions, discretionary waivers and conditional notice rules, not an every-alien crime finding or guaranteed notice/waiver. January 29, 2025 Public Law 119-1 replaces the original Attorney General references in 212(d)(5) with Secretary of Homeland Security and adds the distinct State enforcement route. Original captured 2024 words are preserved with that amending law, not relabeled as the complete unamended 2025 section. Complete captured section 237 retains distinct deportability grounds, actual conviction/knowledge/timing or other own requirements, exceptions/waivers, special nonimmigrant and SIJ boundaries and conditional administrative stays; screening funding does not determine an individual inadmissible, deportable or criminal. The contiguous-return purpose is pursuant to 235(b)(2)(C). The captured 235(b)(2)(C) return authority concerns an applicant for admission whom the examining immigration officer determines is not clearly and beyond a doubt entitled to be admitted, arriving on land (whether or not at a designated port of arrival) from a foreign territory contiguous to the United States. The Attorney General may return that alien to that territory pending a proceeding under section 1229a. The captured parent exceptions for a crewman, an alien to whom paragraph (1) applies, and a stowaway remain. Discretionary return is not a final removal order or universal cross-border return duty. Complete captured 240 proceedings retain judge/charge/exclusive-procedure exceptions, own representation and evidence/examination limits, burdens, decision/appeal, motion and notice/deadline/stay rules. No guaranteed relief, government-paid counsel or individual hearing/return result is inferred. Other H.R.1 immigration components and separately reserved application questions remain unfinished.
- The Senate 90005(b) State Border Security Reinforcement Fund is a distinct DHS fund. Its complete selected operative clauses are retained below. Senate 90005(b) paragraph 1: There is established, in the Department of Homeland Security, a fund to be known as the ``State Border Security Reinforcement Fund.'' Senate 90005(b) paragraph 2: The Secretary of Homeland Security shall use amounts appropriated or otherwise made available for the Fund for grants to eligible States and units of local government for any of the following purposes: Senate 90005(b) purpose A: Construction or installation of a border wall, border fencing or other barrier, or buoys along the southern border of the United States, which may include planning, procurement of materials, and personnel costs related to such construction or installation. Senate 90005(b) purpose B: Any work necessary to prepare the ground at or near land borders to allow construction and maintenance of a border wall or other barrier fencing. Senate 90005(b) purpose C: Detection and interdiction of illicit substances and aliens who have unlawfully entered the United States and have committed a crime under Federal, State, or local law, and transfer or referral of such aliens to the Department of Homeland Security as provided by law. Senate 90005(b) purpose D: Relocation of aliens who are unlawfully present in the United States from small population centers to other domestic locations. Senate 90005(b) paragraph 3: In addition to amounts otherwise available for the purposes described in paragraph (2), there is appropriated for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, to the Department of Homeland Security for the State Border Security Reinforcement Fund established by paragraph (1), $10,000,000,000, to remain available until September 30, 2034, for qualified expenses for such purposes. Senate 90005(b) paragraph 4: The Secretary of Homeland Security may provide grants from the fund established by paragraph (1) to State agencies and units of local governments for expenditures made for completed, ongoing, or new activities, in accordance with law, that occurred on or after January 20, 2021. Senate 90005(b) paragraph 5: Each State desiring to apply for a grant under this subsection shall submit an application to the Secretary containing such information in support of the application as the Secretary may require. The Secretary shall require that each State include in its application the purposes for which the State seeks the funds and a description of how the State plans to allocate the funds. The Secretary shall begin to accept applications not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act. Senate 90005(b) paragraph 6: Nothing in this subsection shall authorize any State or local government to exercise immigration or border security authorities reserved exclusively to the Federal Government under the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1101 et seq.) or the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 101 et seq.). The Federal Emergency Management Agency may use not more than 1 percent of the funds made available under this subsection for the purpose of administering grants provided for in this section. The paragraph (2)(C) alien category retains both unlawful entry and commission of a crime under Federal, State, or local law; those alien predicates do not classify illicit substances. Transfer or referral remains as provided by law. Paragraph (2)(D) instead concerns unlawful presence and relocation from small population centers to other domestic locations; it does not borrow the crime or unlawful-entry predicates from (C), or authorize an international return. Only (A) specifies the southern border; (B) says at or near land borders. The paragraph (2) eligible-State/local-unit grant purpose rule and paragraph (4) discretionary State-agency/local-government expenditure rule remain distinct. The paragraph (5) application obligations name each State; no additional local-government obligation is inferred. The 90-day clause concerns when the Secretary must begin accepting applications, not an applicant deadline or a finding that applications are open. The paragraph (6) construction rule preserves exclusively Federal authorities without deciding which actual functions or expenditures fall within that reservation. The FEMA administration ceiling is discretionary, no more than 1 percent of funds under this subsection for grants in this section; its two scope words remain distinct. This is not an actual award, expenditure, eligibility, individual status/crime, relocation, power delegation or reimbursement determination. House reimbursement amounts, availability, January 21 date and duplicate-reimbursement restriction are not imported. Other package components and the 51 separately reserved application questions remain unfinished.
- Selected Senate 90005(a) funding and its own program context follow. Senate 90005(a) paragraph 1: In addition to amounts otherwise available, there is appropriated to the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, to remain available until September 30, 2029, to be administered under the State Homeland Security Grant Program authorized under section 2004 of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 605), to enhance State, local, and Tribal security through grants, contracts, cooperative agreements, and other activities-- Senate 90005(a) purpose A: $500,000,000 for State and local capabilities to detect, identify, track, or monitor threats from unmanned aircraft systems (as such term is defined in section 44801 of title 49, United States Code), consistent with titles 18 and 49 of the United States Code; Senate 90005(a) purpose B: $625,000,000 for security and other costs related to the 2026 FIFA World Cup; Senate 90005(a) purpose C: $1,000,000,000 for security, planning, and other costs related to the 2028 Olympics; and Senate 90005(a) purpose D: $450,000,000 for the Operation Stonegarden Grant Program. Senate 90005(a) paragraph 2: None of the funds made available under subparagraph (B) or (C) of paragraph (1) shall be subject to the requirements of section 2004(e)(1) or section 2008(a)(12) of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 605(e)(1), 609(a)(12)). The pre-vote fiscal year 2024 DHS/FEMA HSGP notice reproduced on Hawaii's official host describes Operation Stonegarden as supporting enhanced cooperation and coordination among CBP, USBP, and Federal, State, local, Tribal and territorial law enforcement agencies to improve overall border security. It funds joint border-security efforts along routes of ingress and egress to and from international borders, including travel corridors in States bordering Mexico and Canada and States and territories with international water borders. In that notice, those State, local, Tribal and territorial law enforcement agencies use their inherent law enforcement authorities and receive no additional authority from participating in Stonegarden. This is dated program-purpose context, not a new power conferred by the Senate appropriation or a complete 2025 eligibility rule. The additional fiscal year 2025 appropriation names FEMA Administrator, availability until September 30, 2029, administration under the State Homeland Security Grant Program in 6 U.S.C. 605, and State/local/Tribal security through grants, contracts, cooperative agreements and other activities. The Stonegarden purpose is $450,000,000 within that administration provision. The drone-threat, FIFA and Olympics purposes retain their own printed objects and amounts as adjacent context; those purposes alone do not establish an immigration purpose. The exemption from 605(e)(1) minimum allocation and 609(a)(12) grant-administration expense cap expressly names only FIFA paragraph (1)(B) and Olympics paragraph (1)(C); no exemption for Stonegarden paragraph (1)(D) or drone paragraph (1)(A) is inferred. Captured 605(e)(1) retains its State and named-territory minimum-allocation branches, own fiscal-year denominators and percentages; captured 609(a)(12) permits expenses directly related to grant administration except that such expenses may not exceed 3 percent of the grant amount. Neither this cap nor those minima are reclassified as the separate 90005(b) FEMA one-percent ceiling. Complete captured 603, 605 and 609 retain their own program relationships, application/distribution/multistate rules, permitted-use and personnel/construction/recreation restrictions, waivers, reimbursement, transfers and equipment requirements. Their application to a particular 2025 Stonegarden award, including interaction with the dated 2024 notice's separate HSGP components and conditions, is reserved as question 52. No 2024 funding amount, application deadline, performance period, subrecipient tier or approval automatically governs this new appropriation. No particular State/local/Tribal award, entitlement, expenditure, additional law-enforcement power or individual status result is inferred. Other package components and all previously reserved application questions remain unfinished.
- Selected exact Senate 70119 death/disability loan-discharge income-exclusion and SSN provisions follow. Senate 70119 exclusion grounds: In the case of an individual, gross income does not include any amount which (but for this subsection) would be includible in gross income for such taxable year by reason of the discharge (in whole or in part) of any loan described in subparagraph (B), if such discharge was-- (i) pursuant to subsection (a) or (d) of section 437 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 or the parallel benefit under part D of title IV of such Act (relating to the repayment of loan liability), (ii) pursuant to section 464(c)(1)(F) of such Act, or (iii) otherwise discharged on account of death or total and permanent disability of the student. Senate 70119 loan categories: A loan is described in this subparagraph if such loan is-- (i) a student loan (as defined in paragraph (2)), or (ii) a private education loan (as defined in section 140(a) of the Consumer Credit Protection Act (15 U.S.C. 1650(a)). Senate 70119 identification and own marital rules: (i) In general.--Subparagraph (A) shall not apply with respect to any discharge during any taxable year unless the taxpayer includes the taxpayer's social security number on the return of tax for such taxable year. (ii) Social security number.--For purposes of this subparagraph, the term `social security number' has the meaning given such term in section 24(h)(7).. Senate 70119 math-error amendment: Section 6213(g)(2), as amended by this Act, is further amended by striking and at the end of subparagraph (V), by striking the period at the end of subparagraph (W) and inserting , and, and by inserting after subparagraph (W) the following new subparagraph: (X) an omission of a correct social security number required under section 108(f)(5)(C) (relating to discharges on account of death or disability).. Senate 70119 discharge-date applicability: The amendments made by this section shall apply to discharges after December 31, 2025. Each version replaces only 108(f)(5) with the printed exclusion, not all of section 108 or every student-loan tax rule. The original 2024 (5) instead covers its defined discharge categories after December 31, 2020 and before January 1, 2026; the candidate does not silently extend that entire temporary rule unchanged. The common requirement that the discharged loan meet new subparagraph (B) applies across all three ground alternatives. Interaction of that gate, complete loan definitions and the parent-borrower 437(d) reference is reserved as question 55; no blanket conclusion that every HEA discharge qualifies for tax exclusion. Original (f)(1) service-conditioned discharge and (4) named repayment-program exclusions remain separate. New loan categories retain full 108(f)(2) student-loan definition and entire 140(a) private-education definitions, including actual (a)(8) private loan, own private-lender and expense meanings and excluded credit/mortgage categories. This does not mean every education-related debt qualifies. The three exclusion-ground alternatives remain separate: the first two use their specified HEA discharge paths, while only the third prints otherwise discharged on account of death or total and permanent disability of the student. A parent borrower is not silently equated to the student. Full 437(a) retains qualifying loans, death/disability determinations, safeguards, conditional reinstatement, VA documentation and own income-monitoring/approval/opt-out/update rules; 437(d) separately addresses a parent loan when the student dies. Captured 464(c)(1)(F) retains loan-fund agreement scope, borrower death, regulated permanent/total disability, the medically determinable substantial-gainful-activity alternative with its own duration/death tests, and VA unemployability due to service-connected disability. Part D parallel benefit is retained with complete captured 455 and its unless-otherwise-specified limitation, not a universal cancellation promise. Tax exclusion after a qualifying discharge is distinct from authority to cancel a loan. Both versions define the SSN by 24(h)(7), with their own same-bill amended definition and previously bound SSA issuance authority: citizen or the specified authorization route, and issuance before the return due date, not a bare identification number or a citizen-only rule. No child-credit amount or qualifying-child requirement is imported into the loan exclusion. Math-error treatment retains the existing notice and conditional abatement/deficiency procedure, including the 60-day abatement-request path; it is not a fraud finding or actual assessment. The effective date is discharges after December 31, 2025, not taxable years beginning after that date. No individual exclusion, discharge, marital status, SSA-number validity or return result is inferred. Senate requires the taxpayer SSN on the return and does not print the House conditional-spouse requirement or similar-32(d) addition. Those House clauses are not borrowed. Senate further amends the as-amended math-error list by adding (X), not House (W). House application question 54 is not treated as a settled Senate marital rule. Other H.R.1 components and all separately reserved application questions remain unfinished.
- Selected exact Senate account and separate pilot eligibility clauses follow. Senate 70204 IRA treatment with own exceptions: Except as provided in this section or under regulations or guidance established by the Secretary, a Trump account shall be treated for purposes of this title in the same manner as an individual retirement account under section 408(a). Senate 70204 account establishment and instrument: The term `Trump account' means an individual retirement account (as defined in section 408(a)) which is not designated as a Roth IRA and which meets the following requirements: (A) The account-- (i) is created or organized by the Secretary for the exclusive benefit of an eligible individual or such eligible individual's beneficiaries, or (ii) is-- (I) created or organized in the United States for the exclusive benefit of an individual who has not attained the age of 18 before the end of the calendar year, or such individual's beneficiaries, and (II) funded by a qualified rollover contribution. (B) The account is designated (in such manner as the Secretary shall prescribe) at the time of the establishment of the account as a Trump account. (C) The written governing instrument creating the account meets the following requirements: (i) No contribution will be accepted-- (I) before the date that is 12 months after the date of the enactment of this section, or (II) in the case of a contribution made in any calendar year before the calendar year in which the account beneficiary attains age 18, if such contribution would result in aggregate contributions (other than exempt contributions) for such calendar year in excess of the contribution limit specified in subsection (c)(2)(A). (ii) Except as provided in subsection (d), no distribution will be allowed before the first day of the calendar year in which the account beneficiary attains age 18. (iii) No part of the account funds will be invested in any asset other than an eligible investment during any period before the first day of the calendar year in which the account beneficiary attains age 18. Senate 70204 eligible individual and reciprocal election paths: The term `eligible individual' means any individual-- (A) who has not attained the age of 18 before the close of the calendar year in which the election under subparagraph (C) is made, (B) for whom a social security number (within the meaning of section 24(h)(7)) has been issued before the date on which an election under subsection (C) is made, and (C) for whom-- (i) an election is made under this subparagraph by the Secretary if the Secretary determines (based on information available to the Secretary from tax returns or otherwise) that such individual meets the requirements of subparagraphs (A) and (B) and no prior election has been made for such individual under clause (ii), or (ii) an election is made under this subparagraph by a person other than the Secretary (at such time and in such manner as the Secretary may prescribe) for the establishment of a Trump account if no prior election has been made for such individual under clause (i). Senate 70204 account beneficiary: The term `account beneficiary' means the individual on whose behalf the Trump account was established. Senate 70204 full-balance account rollover: For purposes of this section, the term `qualified rollover contribution' means an amount which is paid in a direct trustee-to-trustee transfer from a Trump account maintained for the benefit of the account beneficiary to a Trump account maintained for such beneficiary, but only if the amount of such payment is equal to the entire balance of the Trump account from which the payment is made. Senate 70204 elected child payment: In the case of an individual who makes an election under this section with respect to an eligible child of the individual, such eligible child shall be treated as making a payment against the tax imposed by subtitle A (for the taxable year for which the election was made) in an amount equal to $1,000. Senate 70204 refund to child account: The amount treated as a payment under subsection (a) shall be paid by the Secretary to the Trump account with respect to which such eligible child is the account beneficiary. Senate 70204 pilot birth window, no prior election and citizenship: For purposes of this section, the term `eligible child' means a qualifying child (as defined in section 152(c))-- (1) who is born after December 31, 2024, and before January 1, 2029, (2) with respect to whom no prior election has been made under this section by such individual or any other individual, and (3) who is a United States citizen. Senate 70204 pilot election administration: An election under this section shall be made at such time and in such manner as the Secretary shall provide. Senate 70204 pilot child identification and election-date definition: (1) In general.--This section shall not apply to any taxpayer unless such individual includes with the election made under this section the social security number of the eligible child with respect to whom the election is made. (2) Social security number defined.--For purposes of paragraph (1), the term `social security number' shall have the meaning given such term in section 24(h)(7), determined by substituting `before the date of the election made under section 6434' for `before the due date of such return' in subparagraph (B) thereof. Senate 70204 payment offset exception: Any payment made to any individual under this section shall not be-- (1) subject to reduction or offset pursuant to subsection (c), (d), (e), or (f) of section 6402 or any similar authority permitting offset, or (2) reduced or offset by other assessed Federal taxes that would otherwise be subject to levy or collection. Senate 70204 payment interest start: The period determined under section 6611(a) with respect to any payment under this section shall not begin before January 1, 2028. Senate 70204 mirror-code election: In the case of any possession of the United States with a mirror code tax system (as defined in section 24(k)), this section shall not be treated as part of the income tax laws of the United States for purposes of determining the income tax law of such possession unless such possession elects to have this section be so treated. Senate 70204 pilot account definitions: For purposes of this section, the terms `Trump account' and `account beneficiary' have the meaning given such terms in section 530A(b).. Senate 70204 improper-election penalty and incorporated definitions: In the case of any individual who makes an election under section 6434 with respect to an individual who is not an eligible child of the taxpayer-- (1) if such election was made due to negligence or disregard of the rules or regulations, there shall be imposed a penalty of $500, or (2) if such election was made due to fraud, there shall be imposed a penalty of $1,000. (b) Definitions.-- (1) Eligible child.--The term `eligible child' has the meaning given such term under section 6434. (2) Negligence; disregard.--The terms `negligence' and `disregard' have the same meaning as when such terms are used in section 6662.. Senate 70204 math-error amendment: Section 6213(g)(2), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, is amended by striking and at the end of subparagraph (Y), by striking the period at the end of subparagraph (Z) and inserting , and, and by inserting after subparagraph (Z) the following new subparagraph: (AA) an omission of a correct social security number required under section 6434(e)(1) (relating to the Trump accounts contribution pilot program).. Senate 70204 tax-year applicability: The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025. Senate 70204 Treasury administration appropriation: In addition to amounts otherwise available, there is appropriated to the Department of the Treasury, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, $410,000,000, to remain available until September 30, 2034, to carry out the amendments made by this section. Account creation and pilot contribution eligibility are separate. The account-only clauses above do not print the pilot citizenship test, and the candidate does not import that test to every account. Nor does a trust organized in the United States establish the birthplace or citizenship of an account beneficiary. Each pilot retains its own birth window after December 31, 2024 and before January 1, 2029, qualifying-child reference and account-only payment; a birth window does not mean a United States birthplace. Complete original 152 definitions, exceptions, qualifying-child relationship, residence, age, self-support and joint-return conditions, tie-breakers, divorced-parent alternatives, adoption/foster-child definitions and limited missing-child rule are bound. No automatic parent claim, universal child entitlement or taxpayer citizenship classification is inferred. The defined-number references use their own same-bill 24(h)(7) and complete SSA issuance route, citizen or specified authorization, with each applicable issuance deadline retained. Number validity is distinct from citizenship and from all remaining eligibility requirements. No child-credit amount or earlier loan-exclusion similar-32(d) marital clause is imported into the pilot. Existing notice, 60-day conditional abatement-request and deficiency context remains separate from the new math-error list addition. The new fixed-dollar negligence/fraud alternatives incorporate only 6662 definitions, not its 20-percent penalty; no actual negligence, fraud, assessment or payment is inferred. General retirement/investment/distribution/employer-contribution and unrelated tax mechanics outside the selected clauses remain bound section context, not fully interpreted component claims. Other H.R.1 components and separately reserved application questions remain unfinished. Senate account eligible-individual requirements retain the end-of-election-year under-18 test, defined SSN issued before the election and reciprocal Secretary/person-other-than-Secretary election paths with their own prior-election conditions. The alternative account-creation path requires United States organization, own year-end age test and a qualified rollover that transfers the entire balance. General IRA treatment is subject to new 530A and Secretary regulations/guidance, is not Roth treatment, and is not the House independent trust regime. Senate contributions begin 12 months after enactment, and its distributions use the first day of the age-18 calendar year with own subsection (d) exceptions, not the House birthday/under-25 rule. Pilot separately requires a qualifying child within the birth window, no prior election by this or any other individual and United States citizenship; it does not print House citizenship-at-birth wording. Child SSN accompanies the pilot election with an express before-election substitution in the definition, without House taxpayer/spouse SSNs or a return-only requirement. The separate account before-election condition and unmodified 24(h)(7) return-due-date definition are both retained; actual combined timing/application is reserved as question 57. Tax years beginning after December 31, 2025, account contribution start, interest period not before January 1, 2028 and Treasury $410 million administration availability until September 30, 2034 are separate dates/purposes, not interchangeable child-payment deadlines or benefits.
- Selected exact Senate tips and overtime deduction/identification clauses follow. Senate 70201 deduction and reporting gate: There shall be allowed as a deduction an amount equal to the qualified tips received during the taxable year that are included on statements furnished to the individual pursuant to section 6041(d)(3), 6041A(e)(3), 6050W(f)(2), or 6051(a)(18), or reported by the taxpayer on Form 4137 (or successor). Senate 70201 amount and income limits: (1) In general.--The amount allowed as a deduction under this section for any taxable year shall not exceed $25,000. (2) Limitation based on adjusted gross income.-- (A) In general.--The amount allowable as a deduction under subsection (a) (after application of paragraph (1)) shall be reduced (but not below zero) by $100 for each $1,000 by which the taxpayer's modified adjusted gross income exceeds $150,000 ($300,000 in the case of a joint return). (B) Modified adjusted gross income.--For purposes of this paragraph, the term `modified adjusted gross income' means the adjusted gross income of the taxpayer for the taxable year increased by any amount excluded from gross income under section 911, 931, or 933. Senate 70201 non-employee business-income limit: In the case of qualified tips received by an individual during any taxable year in the course of a trade or business (other than the trade or business of performing services as an employee) of such individual, such qualified tips shall be taken into account under subsection (a) only to the extent that the gross income for the taxpayer from such trade or business for such taxable year (including such qualified tips) exceeds the sum of the deductions (other than the deduction allowed under this section) allocable to the trade or business in which such qualified tips are received by the individual for such taxable year. Senate 70201 qualified-tip conditions: For purposes of this section-- (1) In general.--The term `qualified tips' means cash tips received by an individual in an occupation which customarily and regularly received tips on or before December 31, 2024, as provided by the Secretary. (2) Exclusions.--Such term shall not include any amount received by an individual unless-- (A) such amount is paid voluntarily without any consequence in the event of nonpayment, is not the subject of negotiation, and is determined by the payor, (B) the trade or business in the course of which the individual receives such amount is not a specified service trade or business (as defined in section 199A(d)(2)), and (C) such other requirements as may be established by the Secretary in regulations or other guidance are satisfied. For purposes of subparagraph (B), in the case of an individual receiving tips in the trade or business of performing services as an employee, such individual shall be treated as receiving tips in the course of a trade or business which is a specified service trade or business if the trade or business of the employer is a specified service trade or business. (3) Cash tips.--For purposes of paragraph (1), the term `cash tips' includes tips received from customers that are paid in cash or charged and, in the case of an employee, tips received under any tip-sharing arrangement. Senate 70201 identification: (1) In general.--No deduction shall be allowed under this section unless the taxpayer includes on the return of tax for the taxable year such individual's social security number. (2) Social security number defined.--For purposes of paragraph (1), the term `social security number' shall have the meaning given such term in section 24(h)(7). Senate 70201 own married-individual joint-return rule: If the taxpayer is a married individual (within the meaning of section 7703), this section shall apply only if the taxpayer and the taxpayer's spouse file a joint return for the taxable year. Senate 70201 anti-reclassification regulations: The Secretary shall prescribe such regulations or other guidance as may be necessary to prevent reclassification of income as qualified tips, including regulations or other guidance to prevent abuse of the deduction allowed by this section. Senate 70201 deduction termination: No deduction shall be allowed under this section for any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2028.. Senate 70201 non-itemizer deduction: Section 63(b) is amended by striking and at the end of paragraph (3), by striking the period at the end of paragraph (4) and inserting , and, and by adding at the end the following new paragraph: (5) the deduction provided in section 224.. Senate 70201 math-error amendment: Section 6213(g)(2), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, is amended by striking and at the end of subparagraph (W), by striking the period at the end of subparagraph (X) and inserting , and, and by inserting after subparagraph (X) the following new subparagraph: (Y) an omission of a correct social security number required under section 224(e) (relating to deduction for qualified tips).. Senate 70201 tax-year applicability: The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024. Senate 70202 deduction and reporting gate: There shall be allowed as a deduction an amount equal to the qualified overtime compensation received during the taxable year and included on statements furnished to the individual pursuant to section 6041(d)(4) or 6051(a)(19). Senate 70202 amount and income limits: (1) In general.--The amount allowed as a deduction under this section for any taxable year shall not exceed $12,500 ($25,000 in the case of a joint return). (2) Limitation based on adjusted gross income.-- (A) In general.--The amount allowable as a deduction under subsection (a) (after application of paragraph (1)) shall be reduced (but not below zero) by $100 for each $1,000 by which the taxpayer's modified adjusted gross income exceeds $150,000 ($300,000 in the case of a joint return). (B) Modified adjusted gross income.--For purposes of this paragraph, the term `modified adjusted gross income' means the adjusted gross income of the taxpayer for the taxable year increased by any amount excluded from gross income under section 911, 931, or 933. Senate 70202 qualified-overtime conditions: (1) In general.--For purposes of this section, the term `qualified overtime compensation' means overtime compensation paid to an individual required under section 7 of the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 that is in excess of the regular rate (as used in such section) at which such individual is employed. (2) Exclusions.--Such term shall not include any qualified tip (as defined in section 224(d)). Senate 70202 identification: (1) In general.--No deduction shall be allowed under this section unless the taxpayer includes on the return of tax for the taxable year such individual's social security number. (2) Social security number defined.--For purposes of paragraph (1), the term `social security number' shall have the meaning given such term in section 24(h)(7). Senate 70202 own married-individual joint-return rule: If the taxpayer is a married individual (within the meaning of section 7703), this section shall apply only if the taxpayer and the taxpayer's spouse file a joint return for the taxable year. Senate 70202 regulations: The Secretary shall issue such regulations or other guidance as may be necessary or appropriate to carry out the purposes of this section, including regulations or other guidance to prevent abuse of the deduction allowed by this section. Senate 70202 deduction termination: No deduction shall be allowed under this section for any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2028.. Senate 70202 non-itemizer deduction: Section 63(b), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, is amended by striking and at the end of paragraph (4), by striking the period at the end of paragraph (5) and inserting , and, and by adding at the end the following new paragraph: (6) the deduction provided in section 225.. Senate 70202 math-error amendment: Section 6213(g)(2), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, is amended by striking and at the end of subparagraph (X), by striking the period at the end of subparagraph (Y) and inserting , and, and by inserting after subparagraph (Y) the following new subparagraph: (Z) an omission of a correct social security number required under section 225(d) (relating to deduction for qualified overtime).. Senate 70202 tax-year applicability: The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024. These provisions allow deductions for their own qualified income, not exemption of every dollar described colloquially as tips or overtime and not a guarantee of zero tax. Each retains the complete printed qualified-income gates and its own new statutory subsection references; statements/Form 4137 references, business net-income limits, exceptions and regulatory instructions are not omitted. The original 199A(d)(2) service-business definition is bound with its own 1202/475 references, without importing the separate 199A(d)(3) qualified-business-income phase-in as an automatic tips exception or classifying an actual profession. Overtime means compensation required under FLSA section 7 in excess of the regular rate, not all compensation for hours described as overtime or a taxpayer employment determination. Complete original section 7 with common applicability, regular-rate inclusions/exclusions, alternative arrangements, compensatory-time and other own limitations is bound; no universal 40-hour or all-worker eligibility claim is inferred. All four SSN definitions use their own same-bill 24(h)(7) and full SSA issuance route: citizen or specified authorization, issued before the return due date, not every SSN or a citizen-only rule. Neither a valid number nor filing alone establishes the deduction. Own non-itemizer allowance and math-error amendment remain distinct from existing notice, conditional 60-day abatement-request and deficiency procedure; no actual assessment/fraud determination. All four deduction sections apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024, and deny deductions for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2028; tax-year language is not a discharge/event deadline or repeal of all related reporting/business-credit rules. Other financial/reporting context remains in complete source bindings without an actual implementation conclusion. Other H.R.1 components and separately reserved questions remain unfinished. Senate tips and overtime require taxpayer SSN, without a separately printed House spouse-SSN condition or similar-32(d) addition. Each independently requires a joint return if the taxpayer is married within 7703. Complete original 7703 retains end-of-year or death timing, legal-separation rule and its living-apart alternative requiring a separate return, own household/child/dependency conditions, over-half household costs and no spouse membership during the final six months. No blanket joint filing for every person colloquially described as married. Senate tips caps deduction at $25,000; overtime at $12,500 or $25,000 for a joint return, each with $100 per $1,000 over $150,000/$300,000 MAGI phaseout and own 911/931/933 additions. Senate tips uses own cash/charged/tip-sharing and employee/employer service-business clauses; overtime excludes qualified tips, without importing House highly-compensated/earned-income exclusions. Senate inserts math-error (Y) for tips and (Z) for overtime. No House spouse, similar-marital, compensation-threshold, extra-quote or distinct qualified-tip subsection rule is borrowed.

### Separate choices within one legislative episode

**Compact:** Foushee opposed passage of the complete H.R.4 EH rescission package; no preferred alternative is established. H.R.4 would permanently rescind $800 million of specified Migration and Refugee Assistance unobligated budget authority as part of a wider whole-bill rescission package. Foushee opposed the direct H.R.4 Senate-amendment concurrence and its complete package; no preferred alternative is established. H.Res.590 would directly adopt concurrence in the H.R.4 Senate amendment, including an $800 million Migration and Refugee Assistance unobligated-balance rescission within the full package.

**Detail:**

**house:119:1:168**

Foushee opposed passage of the complete H.R.4 EH rescission package; no preferred alternative is established.

The complete H.R.4 EH final-passage proposal permanently rescinds the named State Migration and Refugee Assistance $800 million unobligated balance in2(b)(7). The House rule499provides a separate final passage and also adopts492engrossment corrections toH.R.1; those separate corrections are not transplanted into this H.R.4 meaning. The affected provision cancels $800 million of UNOBLIGATED budget authority in the Department of State Migration and Refugee Assistance account made available by DivisionA of enacted119-4, effective only on enactment of the proposed rescission package. It does not recover already obligated/executed payments, rescind every fiscal-year balance, eliminate the whole account or establish the actual balance/spending/refugee effect. Existing 119-4 section1101(a)(11)/(b)/(c) carries forward the identified2024State appropriations at their specified levels/authority/conditions;1102–1108preserve extent/manner, comparable multiple/no-year availability, prohibitions and applicable conditions, with enacted State-title anomalies. The complete 2024Migration and Refugee Assistance paragraph appropriates $3.928 billion to remain available until expended, including its $750 million emergency designation and $5 million Israel-resettling refugee allocation, for State to carry out2601(a)/(b), other refugee/migration needs and stated personnel/administrative expenses. Those baseline amounts identify the account framework, not a calculation of the unobligated balance at this vote. Existing 2601(a)/(b) authorizes IOM movement/contributions/participation costs, contributions for specified international refugee-assistance organizations, and presidentially designated assistance to refugees OUTSIDE the United States under the foreign-policy finding. Other refugee/migration needs are stated in the appropriation; the account is not solely an ICE/domestic-removal fund or solely refugee admission quotas.2601(c)Emergency Refugee and Migration Assistance Fund is a separately defined authority, not silently equated to this named account. This proposal rescinds the specified appropriation balance, not the underlying refugee/admission/status statutes, every resettlement benefit or all emergency-assistance authority. It does not alter individual visa, asylum, TPS or sponsor eligibility. The choice is the WHOLE multiaccount rescission package, not a separately recorded vote on the $800 million line, a preferred alternative or a factual judgment about refugees. The entire EH also rescinds listed international-organization/peacekeeping, two Global Health Programs paragraphs, other foreign-assistance/operating accounts and two public-broadcasting fiscal-year amounts. Those are acknowledged as other package choices, not independently interpreted Health/Security/Environment conclusions here. The later Senate replacement changes other account/proviso language and is not assumed part of this earlier June 12vote. No actual rescission, refugee harm/benefit, spending result or enactment is inferred.
